crime_highlights: Mr. Wheatley did board the bus to Vancouver, but became emotionally distressed as he neared the city
he instead went to the Downtown Eastside, where he remained for two days
When he was arrested, Mr. Wheatley had a crack pipe in his possession
rationale_highlights: he suffered intergenerational trauma of the sort not uncommon in such a situation
the importance of Mr. Wheatley's Aboriginal background and the traumas that he suffered growing up appear to have been "lost in the shuffle"
The sentence she imposed was, in my view, unfit as a consequence of this failure
note: Breach offence; harm to victims not applicable.

crime_highlights: the appellant broke the glass door of a public transit bus in the course of a dispute with the bus driver
the appellant stole almost $5,000 worth of jewelry from a business premises
The appellant forced his way into a restaurant in the early morning hours of July 18, 2016, and stole $2,200 in cash and an iPhone
rationale_highlights: The appellant is a 33-year-old significantly disadvantaged Aboriginal offender
the judge noted the appellant's difficult upbringing and personal circumstances and his status as a disadvantaged Aboriginal offender
note: Court never states Aboriginal status reduced sentence; appeal dismissed.

crime_highlights: Cindy Scow was beaten to death by the appellant Mr. Johnny in a dark, abandoned house
she was struck at least six times to the head alone
He told some members of his family that he had beaten up Ms. Scow
Ms. Scow was pronounced dead at the Port Hardy Hospital in the early morning of September 10, 2012
rationale_highlights: Mr. Johnny's mother had grown up in unfortunate circumstances: she is a survivor of the St. Michael's Indian Residential School
Mr. Johnny has a future and his sentence should reflect society's hope for his rehabilitation
the sentence must reflect his circumstances as an Aboriginal offender as required by s. 718.2(e) of the Code
